teaser.text: Vertex Pharmaceuticals sells prescription medicines, most importantly long-term treatments for cystic fibrosis. Its money comes through pharmacies, distributors, hospitals, insurers and government programs, then leaves through manufacturing, partner payments, research, selling and administration.

stock.title: Vertex stock forecast: scenarios through 2029
stock.meta_description: Vertex's forecast weighs a modest weighted outcome against bear and bull paths, with the cash, risks and valuation behind them.
stock.opening: Vertex's weighted outcome is $497.80 in October 2027 and $555.05 in October 2029, with 25% bear, 55% base and 20% bull probabilities. It hinges on CF durability, new-launch conversion and Crinetics execution.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Vertex's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Vertex's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast puts the shares at $497.80 in October 2027, $522.94 in October 2028 and $555.05 in October 2029, with dividends included. Those outcomes represent roughly no return, 5% and 11% from today’s $498.50.
By October 2029, the bear case gives $307.19 and the bull case gives $889.26. The full range is therefore $307.19 to $889.26. The probabilities are 25% bear, 55% base and 20% bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Vertex?

paragraphs.text: By October 2029, CF growth slows as the treated population matures and ALYFTREK switching mostly shifts sales between products. JOURNAVX prescriptions convert slowly into paid use, CASGEVY infusions remain limited by the treatment journey, and Crinetics integration adds debt and execution pressure. The case leads to $375.40 in October 2027 and $307.19 in October 2029. Its probability is 25% because CF remains a durable cash engine, but the newer growth drivers are not yet proven.

New CF starts offset saturation, JOURNAVX becomes routine paid therapy, CASGEVY treatment centers convert more referrals, and Crinetics integrates smoothly. Earnings growth, buybacks and a higher multiple then lead to $610.67 in October 2027 and $889.26 in October 2029. Its probability is 20% because each step carries commercial, clinical or financing risk.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Vertex really make?

paragraphs.text: Net income was $3,953.2 million in 2025. Cash from operations was $3,631.4 million, and after $437.6 million of capital spending, free cash flow was $3,193.8 million. That represented 26.6% of revenue, down from 44.0% in 2022. The business grew, but free cash flow remained below 2023’s $3,278.9 million.

blocks.heading: Did Vertex keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management also delivered a major launch. JOURNAVX received U.S. approval on January 30, 2025, and more than 550,000 prescriptions had been written and filled by year-end. But later commentary pointed to a slower path for normalizing revenue deductions than expected. Delivering a medicine and delivering the expected commercial economics are different achievements.

blocks.heading: What are Vertex's last eight quarters of revenue and profit?

paragraphs.text: Profit grew more slowly. Gross margin declined from 86.3% to 85.3%. Operating income rose to $1,246.9 million from $1,151.1 million, while net income increased to $1,099.8 million. Commercial spending on JOURNAVX and the kidney franchise, together with a higher tax rate, absorbed part of the sales growth.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Vertex's next results?

paragraphs.text: On **November 2, 2026**, Vertex is due to report the first quarterly results after Crinetics closed. Investors should separate growth from the existing business, acquired revenue and the cash consumed by integration and financing.
